description_full: OceanaGold Corporation engages in the exploration, development, and operation of gold and gold/copper mines in the United States, the Philippines, and New Zealand. It explores for gold, copper, and silver deposits. The company was founded in 1990 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

financial_summary: OceanaGold Corporation is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $6.2B market cap on $1.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +25% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +7.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 29%.

The business throws off $541M in free cash flow — roughly 29 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.57× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -10.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 61× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
